processing: After kill-green and rolling the leaf is piled for a long sealed yellowing, then dried. A 2005 laboratory study found the best results at about 7 hours, 35°C and 40% leaf moisture; makers' timings may differ.
harvest_season: Little is documented on the exact picking dates; as with other small-leaf Chinese yellow teas, it is a spring tea.
appearance_wet: Typically tender, even and soft yellow, as with other small-leaf yellow teas.
taste_profile: Rich, sweet fragrance and a mellow body with a cool sweetness.

brewing.notes: General guidance for small-leaf yellow tea. A porcelain gaiwan shows off the colour; ease off on heat if the cup turns flat.

vintage_note: Sold as current-year spring tea, usually by grade. Like most yellow teas it is not an ageing tea, and its aroma fades with time, so ask for the year.
description:
Yuan'an Luyuan is the best-known yellow tea of Yuan'an county in Yichang, Hubei, and the leading example of what is sold as Yuan'an yellow tea. It is named for the Luyuan temple area where it grows.

Its signature is the long piling after rolling. A 2005 laboratory study on Luyuan tea found its best results at about 7 hours, 35°C and 40% leaf moisture, though makers may work differently. This yellowing turns the leaf golden and softens the bite.

Expect apricot-yellow liquor, a rich fragrance and a mellow, cool-sweet cup. Brew below boiling and keep early steeps short.

You may see it sold as Luyuan Maojian, though 'mao jian' more often signals a green tea, so check that the tea is actually yellowed.
history:
The tea is named for the Luyuan temple area where it grows. A Chinese ranking site gives Yuan'an yellow tea, with Luyuan as its best-known form, a history of nearly 800 years; this is a popular account, not a confirmed record.

In modern times the county has promoted itself under the slogan of the first county of Lu Yu's Classic of Tea, and the tea is reported as repeatedly rated a national famous tea, though specific years are not given. It remains a regional tea, often listed among China's main yellow teas.
